decision.observation: 8 mph, gear 1, timer 59:59.000, dots pale. The car has left the gravel and sits on grass to the LEFT of the road, with the gravel clearly to its right and curving up-frame to the right.
decision.hypothesis: Only 1 mph was gained in 1.2 s of throttle while off-road, matching the known grass penalty. The road is to the right, so a single long W+D beat should both build speed and swing the nose back onto the gravel — the pattern that worked off-road before.
decision.memory: Grass gains ~1 mph per 1.2 s of plain throttle here — much slower than gravel, so off-road time must be minimised with long combined steering beats rather than repeated plain throttle.
